```{r}
# Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(e1071)
library(randomForest)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

# Read in Data
breast_cancer_data <- read_csv(here("data/wisconsin_breast_cancer_data.csv"))

# Naive Bayes Model (from previous analysis)
breast_cancer_mod <- naiveBayes(diagnosis ~ ., data = breast_cancer_data)

# Predict diagnosis using Naive Bayes
breast_cancer_data <- breast_cancer_data %>% 
  mutate(predicted_diagnosis_nb = predict(breast_cancer_mod, newdata = .))

# Create the confusion matrix for Naive Bayes
nb_confusion <- breast_cancer_data %>%
  tabyl(diagnosis, predicted_diagnosis_nb) %>%
  adorn_percentages("row") %>%
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 2) %>%
  adorn_ns

print(nb_confusion)

# Investigating False Negatives in Naive Bayes Model
breast_cancer_data <- breast_cancer_data %>%
  mutate(confusion_category_nb = case_when(
    diagnosis == "M" & predicted_diagnosis_nb == "M" ~ "True Positive",
    diagnosis == "M" & predicted_diagnosis_nb == "B" ~ "False Negative",
    diagnosis == "B" & predicted_diagnosis_nb == "B" ~ "True Negative",
    diagnosis == "B" & predicted_diagnosis_nb == "M" ~ "False Positive"
  ))

# Random Forest Model
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
rf_model <- randomForest(diagnosis ~ ., data = breast_cancer_data %>% select(-id, -...33))

# Predict diagnosis using Random Forest
breast_cancer_data <- breast_cancer_data %>%
  mutate(predicted_diagnosis_rf = predict(rf_model, newdata = .))

# Create the confusion matrix for Random Forest
rf_confusion <- breast_cancer_data %>%
  tabyl(diagnosis, predicted_diagnosis_rf) %>%
  adorn_percentages("row") %>%
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 2) %>%
  adorn_ns

print(rf_confusion)

# Investigating False Negatives in Random Forest Model
breast_cancer_data <- breast_cancer_data %>%
  mutate(confusion_category_rf = case_when(
    diagnosis == "M" & predicted_diagnosis_rf == "M" ~ "True Positive",
    diagnosis == "M" & predicted_diagnosis_rf == "B" ~ "False Negative",
    diagnosis == "B" & predicted_diagnosis_rf == "B" ~ "True Negative",
    diagnosis == "B" & predicted_diagnosis_rf == "M" ~ "False Positive"
  ))

# Compare False Negatives between Naive Bayes and Random Forest
false_negatives_comparison <- breast_cancer_data %>%
  filter(confusion_category_nb == "False Negative" | confusion_category_rf == "False Negative") %>%
  select(id, diagnosis, predicted_diagnosis_nb, predicted_diagnosis_rf, confusion_category_nb, confusion_category_rf)

print(false_negatives_comparison)


```
